court: Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit

issues.label: Jurisdiction and finality
issues.why: The court must confirm it has jurisdiction over a final order of removal and any timely petition.

issues.label: Exhaustion of claims
issues.why: The court must determine which arguments were raised to the BIA and are therefore reviewable versus unexhausted.

issues.label: Waiver/forfeiture on review
issues.why: The court must decide whether any issues were inadequately briefed or waived in the petition.

issues.label: Standard of review
issues.why: The court must apply the correct standards (substantial evidence for facts/credibility; de novo for law; abuse of discretion where applicable).

issues.label: Scope of record review
issues.why: The court must confine review to the administrative record and properly treat any new evidence requests.

issues.label: Which decision controls
issues.why: The court must decide whether to review the IJ decision as supplemented by the BIA or the BIA decision alone.

issues.label: Asylum statutory eligibility
issues.why: The court must determine whether applicant meets the refugee definition based on past persecution or well-founded fear on a protected ground.

issues.label: Timeliness of asylum filing
issues.why: Although stated timely, the court must ensure the one-year deadline and any exceptions are properly satisfied.

issues.label: Protected ground nexus
issues.why: The court must decide whether harm was on account of political opinion/party activity (actual or imputed) rather than generalized violence.

issues.label: Persecution threshold
issues.why: The court must assess whether the described beatings, detention, threats, and targeting rise to the level of persecution.

issues.label: Past persecution finding
issues.why: If past persecution is shown, the court must apply the presumption of future persecution and analyze rebuttal.

issues.label: Well-founded fear analysis
issues.why: Absent past persecution, the court must evaluate objective and subjective fear of future persecution.

issues.label: State action attribution
issues.why: The court must determine whether harm was inflicted by government actors (police/military) or by others the government is unwilling/unable to control.

issues.label: Pattern or practice claim
issues.why: The court must consider whether a pattern or practice of persecuting similarly situated opposition activists exists.

issues.label: Credibility legal framework
issues.why: The court must ensure the IJ applied the REAL ID credibility factors and totality-of-circumstances test correctly.

issues.label: Specificity of credibility reasons
issues.why: The court must confirm adverse credibility rests on specific, cogent, record-supported reasons rather than speculation.

issues.label: Materiality of inconsistencies
issues.why: The court must determine whether the four credibility grounds are material or sufficiently probative under governing law.

issues.label: Opportunity to explain discrepancies
issues.why: The court must assess whether applicant was given a fair chance to explain perceived inconsistencies or omissions.

issues.label: Demeanor findings support
issues.why: If demeanor was relied on, the court must check for sufficiently detailed observations and record support.

issues.label: Corroboration requirements
issues.why: The court must decide whether corroboration was reasonably expected, available, and properly evaluated if testimony was questioned.

issues.label: Notice re corroboration
issues.why: The court must consider whether the applicant was put on notice and given opportunity to produce corroboration or explain absence.

issues.label: Weight of documentary evidence
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether the IJ/BIA improperly discounted or failed to consider corroborating documents and country reports.

issues.label: Family members testimony absence
issues.why: The court must consider whether adverse inference from wife’s non-testimony was permissible and whether she was reasonably available.

issues.label: Asylum discretionary denial
issues.why: If statutory eligibility were met, the court must consider whether any discretionary factors were properly addressed.

issues.label: Withholding eligibility standard
issues.why: The court must apply the higher 'more likely than not' standard and determine whether applicant meets it if credible/otherwise proven.

issues.label: Withholding nexus standard
issues.why: The court must apply the correct nexus test for withholding (a protected ground as a central reason or required causal standard per circuit law).

issues.label: CAT legal standard
issues.why: The court must determine whether it is more likely than not the applicant would be tortured if removed.

issues.label: CAT torture definition
issues.why: The court must apply the regulatory definition (severe pain/suffering, intentional, for a proscribed purpose) to the alleged abuses.

issues.label: CAT government acquiescence
issues.why: The court must decide whether torture would be by, or with consent or acquiescence (including willful blindness) of a public official.

issues.label: CAT independent evidence duty
issues.why: Even with adverse credibility, the court must assess whether objective evidence independently establishes CAT risk.

issues.label: Particularized risk assessment
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether evidence shows applicant specifically faces torture, not merely generalized country conditions.

issues.label: Aggregate risk consideration
issues.why: The court must consider risk from all potential torturers cumulatively rather than in isolation.

issues.label: Internal relocation for asylum
issues.why: The court must determine whether applicant can reasonably avoid persecution by relocating within Angola under the correct burden rules.

issues.label: Internal relocation for withholding
issues.why: The court must determine whether internal relocation defeats 'more likely than not' persecution under withholding standards.

issues.label: Internal relocation for CAT
issues.why: The court must consider relocation as part of CAT likelihood analysis, without treating it as a categorical bar.

issues.label: Burden shifting on relocation
issues.why: If persecutor is the government, the court must ensure the presumption against reasonable relocation and proper allocation of proof were applied.

issues.label: Reasonableness of relocation
issues.why: The court must consider practical factors (safety, ability to live, family ties, economic survival) in deciding relocation reasonableness.

issues.label: Past torture relevance to CAT
issues.why: The court must consider whether prior torture at the 'black site' is probative of future torture risk.

issues.label: Threats and post-release targeting
issues.why: The court must decide the legal significance of threats, attempted home visit, and killing/rape of neighbor for future-risk analysis.

issues.label: Country conditions evaluation
issues.why: The court must assess whether reports about Angolan security forces, repression of opposition, and impunity corroborate the claim.

issues.label: Imputed political opinion
issues.why: The court must consider whether authorities would target applicant based on perceived opposition activism even if not a leader.

issues.label: Continuity and changed conditions
issues.why: The court must consider whether conditions or applicant’s profile changed since departure to rebut or support fear/torture likelihood.

issues.label: Pro se fairness safeguards
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether the IJ ensured a fundamentally fair hearing given applicant’s pro se status at merits.

issues.label: Interpreter/communication adequacy
issues.why: If language issues arose, the court must consider whether interpretation/communication problems affected testimony and fairness.

issues.label: Right to present evidence
issues.why: The court must ensure the applicant had a meaningful opportunity to present witnesses, documents, and full testimony.

issues.label: IJ bias or hostility claims
issues.why: If alleged, the court must decide whether IJ conduct created appearance or reality of bias undermining fairness.

issues.label: Due process prejudice standard
issues.why: The court must apply whether any procedural error could have affected the outcome (prejudice).

issues.label: Due process exhaustion
issues.why: The court must decide which due process claims require BIA exhaustion and whether any were exempt as pure constitutional claims.

issues.label: BIA reasoning adequacy
issues.why: The court must assess whether the BIA meaningfully addressed arguments and evidence rather than issuing conclusory affirmance.

issues.label: Remand necessity and scope
issues.why: If error is found, the court must determine appropriate remedy (vacatur/remand) and what issues must be reconsidered.
